colophon: Thus ends the Vishnu Raksha Stotra spoken by Sanatkumara, in the seventy-first chapter of the first part of the Narada Purana.

lines.1: Or else, one should carefully make the protection with Keshava and the other names:
lines.2: may Keshava protect my feet; may Narayana guard my shins;
lines.3: may Madhava protect my hips; Govinda, my secret parts;
lines.4: may Vishnu protect my navel; Madhusudana, my belly;
lines.5: may Trivikrama protect my thighs; may Nara protect my heart;
lines.6: may Shridhara protect my throat, and Hrishikesha my mouth;
lines.7: may Padmanabha protect my chest; may Damodara guard my head.
lines.8: Having placed the names thus on the limbs, at the time of recitation the practitioner
lines.9: becomes fearless of ghosts, vetalas, seizing spirits, and rakshasas.
lines.10: Then, meditating with a collected mind, let him place them once more, with care:
lines.11: in front, may Keshava protect, bearing the discus, shining like river gold;
lines.12: behind, Narayana with the conch, like a dark rain cloud;
lines.13: above, Madhava, dark as the blue lotus, bearing the mace;
lines.14: on the right side, Govinda the archer, great and bright as the moon;
lines.15: to the north, Vishnu bearing the plough, the color of lotus filaments;
lines.16: in the southeast, lotus-eyed Madhusudana with the pestle;
lines.17: Trivikrama, sword in hand, blazing like fire, in the southwest;
lines.18: in the northwest, Madhava with the thunderbolt, bright as the rising sun;
lines.19: in the northeast, lotus-eyed Shridhara, armed with the pattisha blade;
lines.20: may Hrishikesha, bright as lightning, bearing the hammer, protect from above;
lines.21: and below, Padmanabha, radiant as the thousand-rayed sun,
lines.22: bearing every weapon, every power, the first of all, facing every direction.
lines.23: Bright as the indragopa beetle, noose in hand, unconquered, may he protect;
lines.24: may Damodara Hari guard my body, outside and within.
lines.25: Thus, on every side, without a single gap, the cage of the twelve names:
lines.26: I have entered it; no fear of any kind can ever touch me.
lines.27: Having made this protection, a person becomes unassailable;
lines.28: this is the rule held for all the groups of mantras of the Man Lion.
